HUMAN RESOURCES & COMPANY POLICIES
Code of Business Conduct & Ethics
Apex Global Technologies Inc. — Professional Conduct, Communication, and Acceptable Use
Effective Date: January 1, 2026
Version: 5.0
Classification: Confidential — Internal
Owner: Legal & Compliance
1. Purpose and Scope of Application
The Code of Business Conduct and Ethics sets forth the fundamental values, legal requirements, and professional
conduct expectations that govern every director, officer, employee, contractor, and representative of Apex Global
Technologies worldwide. We are committed to conducting business with integrity, transparency, and respect for all
stakeholders.
2. Inclusive Workplace, Anti-Discrimination, and Harassment Prevention
Apex is committed to fostering a safe, diverse, and inclusive working environment free from unlawful discrimination
and harassment:
Equal Opportunity: Employment decisions (hiring, promotion, compensation, termination) are made solely on
individual merit, qualifications, and business needs, without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation,
gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status, or genetic profile.
Harassment-Free Workplace: We strictly prohibit verbal, physical, sexual, visual, or digital harassment. Bullying,
hostile language, offensive jokes, unwelcome advances, and derogatory slurs are subject to immediate
termination.
Mandatory Reporting: Any manager or supervisor who receives a complaint or observes behavior violating this
policy must immediately report it to People Operations or Legal.
3. Conflicts of Interest, Moonlighting, and Outside Activities
Employees must avoid any relationship, investment, or activity that impairs—or appears to impair—their independent
judgment or fidelity to Apex:
Secondary Employment (Moonlighting): Full-time employees may not engage in outside business activities,
consulting, or employment that conflicts with their job responsibilities, utilizes company resources, or competes
directly or indirectly with Apex's products and services. Any outside engagement requires prior written disclosure
and approval from People Operations.
Financial Interests: Employees may not hold significant financial interests in competitors, suppliers, or enterprise
clients without written disclosure to the Chief Compliance Officer.
Gifts and Entertainment: Business courtesies (meals, entertainment, branded gifts) may not exceed $50 in
nominal value and must never be offered or accepted to influence a business decision or government official
(strict compliance with the US Foreign Corrupt Practices Act / UK Bribery Act).
4. Professional Communication and Digital Standards
Corporate Collaboration Channels: Slack, Google Workspace, and GitHub are business tools. Communications
must remain professional, respectful, and constructive at all times.

Public Representation & Media: Employees are not authorized to speak on behalf of Apex to journalists, news
outlets, or media agencies without explicit written authorization from Corporate Communications.
Social Media Usage: When discussing technology, software, or industry topics on personal social channels
(LinkedIn, X/Twitter, personal blogs), employees must state clearly: "The views expressed here are my own and
do not necessarily represent the views of Apex Global Technologies." Never post confidential code, screenshots
of internal dashboards, or client names.
5. Acceptable Use of Company Assets and Intellectual Property
Asset Integrity: Laptops, monitors, networks, and software licenses are provided for business operations.
Incidental personal use is permissible provided it does not interfere with productivity, violate security policies, or
consume excessive network resources.
Software Licensing: Pirated, unverified, or unauthorized third-party software may not be installed on corporate
hardware. All open-source packages must comply with the approved Open Source License Whitelist (Apache 2.0,
MIT, BSD; AGPL/GPLv3 require legal review).
Proprietary Information: Employees must safeguard trade secrets, architecture schemas, customer datasets,
and pricing models. Obligations to protect proprietary information survive termination of employment.
6. Whistleblower Protection and Non-Retaliation Policy
Zero Tolerance for Retaliation
Apex strictly forbids retaliation against any employee who in good faith reports suspected misconduct, policy
violations, or legal non-compliance. Any individual found engaging in retaliatory behavior will be subject to disciplinary
action up to and including immediate termination.
